title: Sell Mineral Rights in Clifton, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Clifton, CO
metaDescription: Clifton sits on Mesa County's Grand Junction fringe, at the western edge of Piceance gas country. See how suburban growth affects your mineral interest's value.
heroLead: Clifton sits just east of Grand Junction in Mesa County, on the western edge of the broader Piceance Basin gas footprint, where suburban growth has increasingly overlapped with land that carries a long history of agricultural mineral severances.
intro: Mesa County's oil and gas history runs deeper than gas alone — the Grand Junction area has also had periods of oil shale interest tied to the Piceance's Green River Formation, though that's a different, largely undeveloped resource from the Williams Fork tight-gas sands that drove actual drilling activity elsewhere in the basin. Most producing mineral interests near Clifton, where they exist, connect to the tight-gas trend rather than the oil shale story, which has stayed mostly speculative for decades.

sections.heading: Suburban growth limiting new surface access
paragraphs: As Clifton has grown as a Grand Junction suburb, new drilling within its built-up areas has become less practical, similar to the pattern in Front Range suburbs, even though the surrounding rural Mesa County land still sees selective gas leasing. A mineral interest tied to a Clifton legal description is more likely to be non-producing or connected to an older well than to recent activity.

sections.heading: Don't confuse oil shale hype with actual production value
paragraphs: Mesa County has periodically attracted attention over its oil shale potential, and it's worth being clear that oil shale extraction has never become commercially viable at scale in Colorado despite decades of periodic interest. We price mineral interests off actual, realistic gas production and leasing activity, not speculative oil shale development that hasn't materialized.

sections.heading: What we check for a Clifton tract
paragraphs: We confirm your legal description against current lease and unit filings, review any production history, and check the Mesa County Clerk and Recorder's deed record for your exact decimal interest. Given the mix of suburban and rural land in this area, we don't apply a flat number and instead evaluate each tract on its specific position.

faqs.question: Does oil shale potential add value to my Clifton-area minerals?
faqs.answer: We don't price interests off oil shale speculation, since it's never reached commercial-scale development in Colorado despite decades of periodic interest. Value is based on realistic gas production and leasing activity.

faqs.question: Is there active gas leasing near Clifton?
faqs.answer: Selectively in the surrounding rural county, less so within the built-up suburban area. We check current filings against your specific legal description.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my exact ownership share?
faqs.answer: We can pull your deed and probate history from the Mesa County Clerk and Recorder to confirm your decimal interest.
